draft.title: Stereotypes and archetypes
card: an oversimplified idea of a type of person, which treats everyone in a group as the same. A story that shows every teenager as lazy and glued to a phone is using a stereotype.
a character pattern found across many stories, such as the mentor who guides the hero, or the trickster who causes trouble with clever tricks.
Writers often start with a stereotype or an archetype and then add detail. A mentor who is also nervous and funny feels like a real person, not a pattern.

Stereotypes can be unfair, because they ignore how different people in a group really are. Archetypes are patterns of role and behaviour, so readers recognise them in stories from many times and places.
draft.remember: A stereotype oversimplifies a group of people. An archetype is a pattern repeated across many stories.

a.q: Which description best defines an archetype?
opts: A character pattern that appears in many different stories
An oversimplified idea that treats a group as all alike
A character who changes a great deal during one story
A character who tells the reader directly what they are like
a.why: An archetype is a pattern, such as the mentor, that readers meet again and again across stories. The second option describes a stereotype, which is the tempting mix-up.
a.clue: Think of a pattern seen in many stories, not an idea about a group.

b.q: In a novel, every farmer is shown as slow, scruffy and not clever, and no farmer is ever shown any other way. What is this?
opts: A stereotype, because it oversimplifies a type of person
An archetype, because it appears in many characters
A stereotype, because it shows a character who changes
An archetype, because it guides the hero through the story
b.why: Every farmer is given the same few traits, which oversimplifies a type of person. That is a stereotype. It is not an archetype, because it is not a story role such as the mentor, and appearing many times in one book does not make a pattern an archetype.
b.clue: Does it treat a whole group as the same?

a.best: A character pattern that appears in many different stories

b.best: A stereotype, because it oversimplifies a type of person
